summary: Scheduled alert evaluation times out when dashboards include very large inline JSON panels
description: Issue summary: ParcelFlow reports scheduled alerts linked to a dashboard fail to evaluate on schedule. The scheduler marks the job as timed out, and the alert window is missed. Impact: Customers on dedicated capacity miss alert notifications for production SLOs; manifests as no Slack/webhook messages and alert state not updated in console. Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated tenant for ParcelFlow. First seen: 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC; recurring each day around the scheduled 02:00 UTC rolling window. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a dashboard with multiple panels including a single 'JSON / Debug' panel that contains a ~12MB inline JSON payload (copy/paste from logs). 2) Attach an alert to a panel on that dashboard with evaluation window aligned to the dashboard's time range and enable 'Evaluate on schedule'. 3) Schedule the alert to run at 02:00 UTC. 4) Observe scheduler logs and alert state after scheduled run. Expected: scheduled alert evaluates, updates status, and sends notifications if triggered. Observed: scheduler worker reports evaluation timeout after 45s (scheduler configured timeout = 30s), alert status remains stale, no notifications sent. Additional notes: ad-hoc manual evaluation via console works when the inline JSON panel is removed. The same dashboard with smaller JSON payloads (<1MB) evaluates normally. Logs/trace snippets: "scheduler.job[alert-eval].time=2026-03-09T02:00:12Z status=timeout duration=45s reason=panel-renderer-hang trace_id=tr-93abf". Attachments: dashboard-export.json (redacted), scheduler logs excerpt (attached to ticket).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:21 - Evelyn Carter: Customer reported recurring misses for scheduled alerts after their nightly log ingestion. They confirmed the dashboard contains a large inline JSON panel used for developer debugging.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Support Engineer Marco Li: Acknowledged. I've reproduced locally on staging using a 10MB inline JSON panel; scheduler worker logs show worker blocked in panel rendering step and then hit the 30s evaluation timeout. Assigning to infra-alerting team for deeper analysis.

2026-03-11 14:42 - SRE Priya Nair: Initial hypothesis: dashboard renderer runs synchronously in the alert evaluation path, and large panels can block the evaluation event loop. Experimented with isolating 'render-only' panels in a separate headless renderer process and saw evals complete. Opening an internal ticket to decouple heavy panel rendering from alert evaluation.

2026-03-12 11:10 - Marco Li: Reached out to ParcelFlow to request a sanitized example of the JSON payload and confirm whether they can switch to referencing a saved query instead. Customer agreed to test a snapshot of the dashboard without the JSON panel; they reported scheduled alerts resumed normally.

2026-03-12 16:30 - Engineering Lead Aisha Patel: Planning a short-term mitigation and a medium-term fix. Short-term: increase scheduler per-job timeout for tenants affected by large-panel dashboards and add a rendering time budget. Medium-term: move heavy panel rendering to async pre-render pipeline and cache rendered artifacts so alert evals can operate on cached outputs.
investigation_notes: Checked scheduler logs (prod-us-east) for affected tenant: multiple consecutive eval timeouts aligned to customer's schedule window.
Reproduced on staging by pasting a 11.8MB JSON into a dashboard JSON panel; ad-hoc manual evaluation works if run interactively but scheduled job times out consistently.

Profiling of alert-eval worker shows 85% CPU spent inside dashboard-renderer.parseAndRender() for large JSON panels; stack traces point to synchronous JSON pretty-print and DOM-to-image conversion blocking the worker thread.
Confirmed removing the large panel or replacing it with a reference to a lightweight saved query returns evaluation latency to normal (<5s).

Verified existing retention/compaction jobs unaffected; this is unrelated to retention layer but interacts with scheduler because rendering uses cached query results that are larger when retention window increases.
Related PR identified that introduced synchronous rendering in eval path: github.com/redwood-inference/console@commit/9b7e4f3 (linked above).
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation rolled out 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC to prod-us-east for affected dedicated tenants: scheduler per-job timeout increased from 30s to 60s and a rendering time budget guard was added to fail fast on heavy panels. Nightly monitor added to watch for increased eval durations.
Medium-term plan: implement async pre-render pipeline for heavy panels and a cache keyed by panel hash + time window. Target ETA for staged rollout: 2026-04-20. Issue tracked internally in INT-33012.

Customer communication: ParcelFlow informed of short-term mitigation and asked to remove large inline payloads; they accepted and confirmed alerts resumed. Follow-up scheduled for 2026-03-18 to validate metric stability.
Post-deploy verification: two scheduled runs observed post-mitigation with durations 9s and 12s; no timeouts and alerts evaluated as expected.

Follow-ups: (1) Add console UI warning when saving panels with inline payloads >2MB recommending saved queries or attachments; (2) Add alerting doc note about heavy panels impacting scheduled evaluations.
